matched_rules.because: Storms are active (lightning caused voltage swells), a portion of the datacenter transferred to generator power, and mechanical cooling shut down despite surge suppressors.

Mechanical cooling is down, the datacenter is running on its load-dependent thermal buffer, and storage servers began shutting down due to unsafe temperatures, indicating buffer depletion and automated shutdown.

next_actions.action: Immediately verify that mechanical cooling systems are still running, rather than assuming surge suppressors protected them.
If mechanical cooling has shut down, treat the datacenter as being on a load-dependent thermal buffer and start planning for its depletion.
Transfer the rest of the datacenter to generators to stabilize the power supply while storms are still active.
Treat the thermal buffer as a finite resource and act before it is depleted.
Expect that once the buffer is gone, temperature will exceed safe operational thresholds and automated device shutdown will begin.
Recognize that in parts of the datacenter temperature can rise so quickly that hardware is damaged before it can shut down.

escalate.to: facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer
escalate.reason: Mechanical cooling confirmed shut down while storms remain active in the area (R-001 trigger).

not_covered: No rule addresses the specific scenario of lightning-induced voltage swells causing both a power transfer and a cooling shutdown despite surge suppressors, while the datacenter is still on a load-dependent thermal buffer and customer impact has begun. The pill's rules cover related aspects but do not fully encompass this combination of signals.

per_finding.note: R-001 explicitly names lightning-induced voltage swells shutting down mechanical cooling despite surge suppressors.
R-002 directs treating the thermal buffer as finite and expecting automated shutdown once safe thresholds are exceeded.
R-002 next action states temperature can rise so quickly that hardware is damaged before it can shut down.
R-001 next action directs transferring the rest of the datacenter to generators while storms are active.
Triage does not mention storage servers, network devices, or power units being damaged.
No rule calls for forensic analysis of hardware or review of recovery procedures.
No rule addresses evaluating future hardware design of storage scale units for environmental resiliency.
